
### ECN  {.smaller}


* explicit congestion notification 
<hr class="vspace" />
* when buffer ‘close’ to full
* switches set ‘congestion experienced’ (CE) signal in some packets
* goal: congestion signal <i>instead of</i> packet drops 

   * avoid all the retransmission, hopefully
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* still have fallback to dropping packets


### ECN and TCP/IP  {.smaller}


* congestion experience (CE) signal in IP heaer
* when ACKing, ‘‘return’’ CE signal with ACK 

   * ECN echo (ECE) TCP flag on ACK packets
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* when sender sees ECE flag, confirm reciept by setting ‘‘congestion window reduced’’ (CWR) flag until ECE flag stops being set


### ECN opt-in  {.smaller}


* two bits in IP header
* RFC 3168 says: 
<hr class="vspace" />
* <code>00</code> = not-ECN capable (default)
* <code>01</code>, <code>10</code> = ECN-capable (set by TCP/etc. implementation)
* <code>11</code> = congestion experienced


### ECN timeline  {.smaller}

![](/congest-opt/texfig/ecn-timeline.figure.svg)
 

* data sent has place for ECN bit to be placed
* switch modifies ECN bit <em>if buffer close to full</em>
* ACK indicates if ECN bit was set


### reacting to ECN marks 


* multiple options for using ECN marks
* simplest idea: 
<hr class="vspace" />
* adjust window as if packet was dropped
* … but don't need to resend data


### ECN deployment  {.smaller}


* ECN proposed in 2001
* 13 years later: around 56% support on websites[^trammel]
* 16 years later:  

   * around 80% support on websites[^kuhlewind]
   * around 0.2% of servers disallow connection when ECN requested

* 20 years later: 

   * around 86% support on websites[^lim]
   * around 4% of paths strip ECN signals, including notable ISPs/cloud providers/etc.
   * around 7.5% of connections (from sampled Universities) enable ECN

[^trammel]: Trammel et al, ‘‘Enabling Internet-Wide Deployment of Explicit Congestion Notification’’
[^kuhlewind]: Kühlewind et al, ‘‘Tracing Internet Path Transparency’’
[^lim]: Lim et al, ‘‘A Fresh Look at ECN Traversal in the Wild’’

### example: DCTCP  {.smaller}


* DataCenter TCP (2010)
* intended for datacenters 

   * high bandwidth, low latency networks

* based on explicit congestion notification
* … but uses different multiplicative decrease strategy 
<hr class="vspace" />
* measure portion of packets marked recently $\alpha$
* decrease by factor of $1-\alpha/2$ 

   * respond gradually to congestion
   * start responding early (packets marked when queues far from full)
